name: Dolly Parton
description:
'''Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean''' ({{nee|'''Parton'''}}; January 19, 1946 – August 25, 2026) was an American singer-songwriter, actress, philanthropist, and businesswoman. Dubbed the "[[Queen of Country]]", Parton was one of the most successful performers in the history of [[country music]]. She was also known for [[Cultural impact of Dolly Parton|her cultural influence]], particularly through [[Dollywood]] and [[#Education and literacy|the Dollywood Foundation]]. With more than a hundred million records sold, Parton was among the [[best-selling music artists]] in history.

Born and raised in [[East Tennessee]], Parton wrote her first song at age six, performed regularly on television by age ten, made her first recording a year later, and became a professional songwriter at sixteen. After writing songs for others, she released her debut album, ''[[Hello, I'm Dolly]]'' in 1967, starting her nearly sixty-year career. Parton released [[Dolly Parton albums discography|49 studio albums]] and wrote more than 3,000 songs, including "[[I Will Always Love You]]"{{snd}}a two-time US country chart-topper and [[I Will Always Love You (Whitney Houston recording)|an international success]] for [[Whitney Houston]] that became the [[best-selling single]] by a woman{{snd}}"[[Jolene]]", "[[Coat of Many Colors (song)|Coat of Many Colors]]", and "[[9 to 5 (Dolly Parton song)|9{{nbs}}to{{nbs}}5]]". The lattermost, as well as the [[Kenny Rogers]] duet "[[Islands in the Stream (song)|Islands in the Stream]]", reached No.{{nbs}}1 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot{{nbs}}100]]. Her final solo studio album, ''[[Rockstar (Dolly Parton album)|Rockstar]]'' (2023), became her highest-charting album on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard''{{nbs}}200]], reaching No.{{nbs}}3.

Parton starred in the comedy films ''[[9 to 5 (film)|9 to 5]]'' (1980), ''[[The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas (film)|The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas]]'' (1982), ''[[Rhinestone (film)|Rhinestone]]'' (1984), ''[[Steel Magnolias]]'' (1989), ''[[Straight Talk]]'' (1992), and ''[[Joyful Noise (film)|Joyful Noise]]'' (2012). She produced and starred in a series of [[Netflix]] features including ''[[Christmas on the Square]]'' (2021), which earned her a [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Movie|Primetime Emmy Award]]. She also played [[Aunt Dolly]] in ''[[Hannah Montana]]'' (2006–2010), hosted ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' (1989), and guest-starred on ''[[Reba (TV series)|Reba]]'' (2005) and ''[[Grace and Frankie]]'' (2022). She wrote the music and lyrics for [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]]'s ''[[9 to 5 (musical)|9{{nbs}}to{{nbs}}5]]'' (2009), which earned her a [[Tony Award]] nomination. Her life will be depicted in ''[[Dolly: A True Original Musical]]'' (2026).

Parton's music received 52 gold, platinum, and multi-platinum certifications from the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA). [[List of awards and nominations received by Dolly Parton|Her accolades]] include eleven [[Grammy Awards]] and three [[Emmy Awards]]. She logged 25 [[Timeline of Billboard number-one country songs|No.{{nbs}}1 ''Billboard'' country singles]] (tied with [[Reba McEntire]] for the most by a woman), 44 career [[Top Country Albums|Top{{nbs}}10 country albums]] (a record for any artist), and 110 career-charted singles over forty years. Parton was honored with a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]] (1984), the [[National Medal of Arts]] (2004), the [[Kennedy Center Honor]] (2006), the [[Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award]] (2011), and the [[Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award]] (2025).
